title: poison() uses derived key instead of zeroing - security wipe fails
description:
Root Cause: The poison() method at line 202-208 in responder.rs replaces the private key with a key derived from a zero seed: let (zero_priv, zero_pub) = SigningKey::from_seed(&[0; KEY_LEN_32]); self.privkey = zero_priv;. However, SigningKey::from_seed calls schnorr48::derive_keypair, which performs cryptographic key derivation and does NOT produce zero bytes. The derived key has non-zero bytes [80, 70, 173, ...] rather than [0, 0, 0, ...].

Affected Test: responder_post_dh_failure_wipes_and_poison_state (line 840 expects privkey.as_bytes() == [0; 32])

Location: /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/oscore/src/edhoc/responder.rs lines 202-208

Suggested Fix: Change the poison() method to call self.privkey.zeroize() instead of replacing with a derived key. The SigningKey struct already derives Zeroize (sign.rs line 23), and the underlying schnorr48::PrivateKey([u8; 32]) also derives Zeroize (schnorr48/src/keys.rs line 59), so this will properly zero the key bytes. Replace lines 203-204 with: self.privkey.zeroize(); and remove the pubkey replacement (public keys do not need wiping for security).

Error Type: Logic error - security-sensitive key zeroization is not working correctly
